scenarios.explanation: Build flags from the two independent choices, place -- before the filename, and run the quoted list. Quoting preserves the filename as one value; -- tells the selected utility it is an operand. The single - remains a stdin marker and is rejected before running anything. Direct supported branches that produce the same behavior are equally valid.
hints: Treat the order and duplicate policy as separate choices. Check the argument count and recognized values before invoking a tool.
Start with command=(sort), then add -r and/or -u only for the requested choices. Use -- before the source operand.
Run the whole list with "${command[@]}". Do not join it into one string or use the source as a printf format. Reject - before the utility can read stdin.
scenarios.simplifications: Bash-specific dense arrays and the disclosed in-process shell subset; equivalent supported direct branches are accepted. No eval, sourcing, external/PATH command lookup or host execution. Only flat simulated /work text files and fixed C/POSIX byte-order sort/uniq/cut flags exist. -- separates these utilities' options; - still denotes stdin. initial.source: # Build a configurable sort request without treating a filename as flags.

cases.name: Ascending with every entry
Unique entries from an option-looking name
Descending while keeping repeated entries
Descending unique and a literal double-hyphen name
Empty source
Literal spaces patterns percent and UTF8
Absent source
Unknown ordering
Unknown duplicate policy
Extra argument
A single hyphen is not a source name
Missing source argument

solution:
invalid() { printf 'Usage: manifest asc|desc all|unique SOURCE\n' >&2; }
if test "$#" -ne 3; then invalid; exit 2; fi
order=$1
policy=$2
source=$3
case "$order" in asc|desc) : ;; *) invalid; exit 2 ;; esac
case "$policy" in all|unique) : ;; *) invalid; exit 2 ;; esac
case "$source" in ''|-|.|..|*/*) invalid; exit 2 ;; esac
if test -f "$source"; then :; else printf 'Missing source: %s\n' "$source" >&2; exit 1; fi
LC_ALL=C
command=(sort)
if test "$order" = desc; then command=("${command[@]}" -r); fi
if test "$policy" = unique; then command=("${command[@]}" -u); fi
command=("${command[@]}" -- "$source")
"${command[@]}"

teaching.prerequisite_note: Use quoted arrays and replacement from “Repair a queue that loses its tail”, C-locale sorting, case guards and basename checks from earlier units. This lesson adds executing a command list and separating options from filenames.

concepts.title: A command has separate words
concepts.text: A command starts with the program name; later words are its arguments. command=(sort -r -- "-shelf") stores four separate words. Running "${command[@]}" uses that first word as the program name and passes the other entries separately. This array spelling is Bash-specific, not portable sh.

concepts.title: Build optional parts without flattening text
concepts.text: command=(sort) starts a new command. command=("${command[@]}" -r) copies its current entries, then adds one flag. The right-hand side uses the old list before replacement. Quoting the whole @ expansion preserves spaces, empty entries and literal wildcard characters.

concepts.title: A quoted name can still look like an option
concepts.text: Quotes keep "-shelf" as one argument; they do not stop a utility from seeing an option. For the sort, uniq and cut commands used here, -- ends the options. Put the source filename after it. A single - still means standard input, even after --, so these assignments reject it as a source.

concepts.title: Choose behavior from a small known set
concepts.text: Select program names and flags from your own case branches. Do not treat a supplied command string as a program. Text such as $(printf surprise) inside an argument stays data when expanded; it is not parsed again as script syntax. Quoted arrays do not choose safe operations for you.

concepts.title: Keep ordering and duplicate policy independent
concepts.text: The simulator's tools use fixed C/POSIX byte ordering. sort prints ascending text; -r reverses it and -u removes repeated whole lines. Combine -r and -u when both are requested. LC_ALL=C selects this supported locale here; it does not model sending variables to separate programs. In real Bash, sending a newly created LC_ALL variable to an external program needs export or a command-prefix assignment. Those forms are outside this simulator. The lab supplies arguments and files; create command, order and policy yourself.

teaching.example:
command=(sort)
if test "$1" = reverse; then command=("${command[@]}" -r); fi
command=("${command[@]}" -- "$2")
LC_ALL=C
"${command[@]}"
teaching.inputs: Arguments are reverse and -shelf. The separate museum shelf has Map, Atlas, Map; museum-preserve.txt is unchanged. This example uses different interface values and files from the assignment.

scenarios.summary: Choose the right text tool per job and report failures without losing later work.
scenarios.objective:
Accept one or more OP SOURCE pairs. With zero pairs or an unpaired final argument, print only Usage: transform OP SOURCE ... and a newline on standard error; return 2 and process no jobs.

Process pairs in order. ordered sorts all lines in C/POSIX byte order; neighbors collapses only adjacent identical lines; owners prints field 3 of colon-containing lines, skipping notes without a colon and keeping empty owner fields. For a valid job print Job N: OP and a newline, then the exact transformation output. Number every pair, starting at 1.

Unknown OP prints Rejected job N: unknown operation. An empty SOURCE, a directory part, . , .. or - prints Rejected job N: invalid source. An absent valid source prints Missing source for job N: SOURCE. Send each diagnostic to standard error with a newline, with no heading for that failed job, then process later jobs. Return 1 if any job failed, otherwise 0. Change no files. Source names may begin with hyphens. Use the supplied filenames exactly.

scenarios.explanation: An approved operation chooses a tool; it is not a program supplied by the request. Start a fresh command list per pair, validate before the heading, and remember errors while later pairs run. Neighbor deduplication must keep separated repeats. Print a heading only for a validated job. Keep a failed flag, and advance exactly two arguments for every pair.
Replace the old command list for each job. ordered, neighbors and owners need different arguments; use -- before the chosen filename.

initial.source: # Process each approved transformation and keep later jobs after a rejection.

cases.name: Three different transformations
cases.stdout:
Job 1: ordered
a
a
z
Job 2: neighbors
b
a

Job 3: owners

cases.name: One ordering job from a flag-looking source
Owner fields keep literal text
Empty source is a successful job
Unknown middle job does not hide the last job
cases.stdout:
Job 1: ordered
a
a
z
Job 3: neighbors
b
a

cases.name: Missing middle source then a valid job
cases.stdout:

a
a
z
Job 3: owners

cases.name: Single hyphen rejected without ending the batch
An unpaired final argument is rejected before work
No pairs supplied
Empty source argument
Text resembling shell code is not an operation
Repeated source with different meanings
cases.stdout:
Job 1: neighbors
z
a
z
Job 2: ordered
a
a
z
z

solution:
count=$#
if test "$count" -eq 0 || test "$((count % 2))" -ne 0; then
 printf 'Usage: transform OP SOURCE ...\n' >&2; exit 2
fi
LC_ALL=C
number=0
failed=0
while test "$#" -gt 0; do
 number=$((number + 1))
 action=$1
 file=$2
 shift 2
 ready=yes
 command=()
 case "$action" in
  ordered) command=(sort) ;;
  neighbors) command=(uniq) ;;
  owners) command=(cut -s -d ':' -f 3) ;;
  *) printf 'Rejected job %s: unknown operation\n' "$number" >&2; ready=no; failed=1 ;;
 esac
 if test "$ready" = yes; then
  case "$file" in ''|-|.|..|*/*) printf 'Rejected job %s: invalid source\n' "$number" >&2; ready=no; failed=1 ;; esac
 fi
 if test "$ready" = yes; then
  if test -f "$file"; then :; else
   printf 'Missing source for job %s: %s\n' "$number" "$file" >&2; ready=no; failed=1
  fi
 fi
 if test "$ready" = yes; then
  command=("${command[@]}" -- "$file")
  printf 'Job %s: %s\n' "$number" "$action"
  "${command[@]}"
 fi
done
exit "$failed"

teaching.prerequisite_note: Use the previous command-list lesson, adjacent repeat handling, cut fields, function return and small-count arithmetic. This lesson combines a closed tool allowlist with independent job processing.

concepts.title: Pick the tool before running it
concepts.text: A case decision can build a different known command list for each operation. In the museum example, titles selects sort and shelves selects cut. The default branch rejects an unrecognized request. Never use the request itself as an unrestricted program name.

concepts.title: Start a new list for each job
concepts.text: Each new job needs its own program and arguments. Replace the previous command list with command=(sort), command=(uniq), or the appropriate cut words. Appending a new program to the old list would pass it as an argument to the old program. Two jobs may name the same source and still need different work.

concepts.title: Neighboring repeats and sorted repeats differ
concepts.text: uniq collapses only adjacent identical lines. The sequence A, A, B, A becomes A, B, A. Sorting first would change the meaning. sort keeps all entries unless -u is explicitly chosen. cut -s -d ":" -f 3 keeps field 3 from colon-containing lines, including an empty field; it skips lines without a colon.

concepts.title: Reject one job while finishing the batch
concepts.text: Check a job before printing its heading or running its tool. Use a variable such as failed=1 to remember a rejected job, then continue to the next pair. A function may return 1 for that job; exit would end the entire script. Read a command status before a later command replaces it.

concepts.title: Validate the pair interface before starting
concepts.text: An operation and source form one pair. With count=$#, test "$((count % 2))" -ne 0 detects an odd count: % is the remainder after division. This uses the known small argument count, not arbitrary numeric text. shift 2 removes the pair just processed. Keep filename operands after -- and reject the single - source. The lab supplies argument pairs and files; action, file, command and failed are variables you create.

cases.name: Bad final operation cannot publish earlier work
Bad final source cannot truncate the destination
Destination is an input
Protected destination
Unknown publication mode
No transformation jobs
Single hyphen cannot consume standard input
Destination traversal is rejected

solution:
invalid() { printf 'Invalid transformation plan\n' >&2; }
if test "$#" -lt 4; then invalid; exit 2; fi
mode=$1
destination=$2
shift 2
count=$#
if test "$((count % 2))" -ne 0; then invalid; exit 2; fi
case "$mode" in preview|apply) : ;; *) invalid; exit 2 ;; esac
case "$destination" in ''|-|.|..|*/*|keep.txt) invalid; exit 2 ;; esac
LC_ALL=C
prepare() {
 local number=0
 local action
 local file
 local command
 local result
 while test "$#" -gt 0; do
  number=$((number + 1))
  action=$1
  file=$2
  shift 2
  case "$file" in ''|-|.|..|*/*) return 2 ;; esac
  if test "$file" = "$destination"; then return 2; fi
  if test -f "$file"; then :; else return 2; fi
  command=()
  case "$action" in
   ordered) command=(sort) ;;
   neighbors) command=(uniq) ;;
   owners) command=(cut -s -d ':' -f 3) ;;
   *) return 2 ;;
  esac
  command=("${command[@]}" -- "$file")
  if result=$("${command[@]}"); then :; else return 2; fi
  printf 'Job %s: %s\nResult: <%s>\n' "$number" "$action" "$result"
 done
}
if plan=$(prepare "$@"); then :; else invalid; exit 2; fi
if test "$mode" = preview; then
 printf 'Preview\n%s\n' "$plan"
else
 printf '%s\n' "$plan" > "$destination"
 printf 'Published %s jobs to %s\n' "$((count / 2))" "$destination"
fi

teaching.prerequisite_note: Use the previous mixed-job lesson, command substitution, helper status and validated preview/publication. This capstone adds no new shell syntax; the work is combining those checks before any visible publication.

concepts.title: Prepare results before publishing them
concepts.text: The assignment combines different transformations, not just filenames. Validate every operation and source before showing a plan or changing a destination. A bad final job must not leave a partially published report. Existing source and protected files must stay unchanged.

concepts.title: Capture text and check the status
concepts.text: result=$(transform labels) captures the helper's standard output. Capture removes newline bytes at the end while keeping newlines inside the text. if result=$(transform labels); then ...; else ...; fi also checks the helper's status. A failed preparation is not a publishable result.

concepts.title: Separate a job result from the complete plan
concepts.text: Each job contributes a numbered heading and a Result: <VALUE> line. VALUE may contain internal newlines; an empty result gives Result: <>. Build the complete plan first. When a final capture removes its ending newline, printf '%s\n' "$plan" restores the one required final line break.

concepts.title: Preview and apply have different effects
concepts.text: Preview prints the prepared plan and leaves all files alone. Apply replaces only the chosen destination and prints a short confirmation. Reject a destination equal to any source or keep.txt, and reject directory parts, empty names, . , .. and -. This is flat simulated-file replacement, not crash-safe filesystem publication.

concepts.title: Keep the request separate from the command
concepts.text: The helper still uses closed case branches to select sort, uniq or cut, then a quoted argument list and --. The operation name is not arbitrary code. Supplied text, spaces and percent signs stay data with fixed printf formats. The example's gallery variables are created by the example; the lab supplies only the documented assignment arguments/files.

teaching.example:
transform() {
 case "$1" in
  labels) command=(sort -u -- gallery-labels.txt) ;;
  rooms) command=(cut -s -d ':' -f 2 -- gallery-rooms.txt) ;;
  *) return 2 ;;
 esac
 "${command[@]}"
}
LC_ALL=C
if labels=$(transform labels); then :; else printf 'Gallery unavailable\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
if rooms=$(transform rooms); then :; else printf 'Gallery unavailable\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
plan="Labels: <$labels>
Rooms: <$rooms>"
mode=$1
if test "$mode" = review; then
 printf 'Gallery preview\n%s\n' "$plan"
else
 printf '%s\n' "$plan" > gallery-result.txt
 printf 'Gallery saved\n'
fi
teaching.inputs: The argument is review. Separate gallery files supply labels and rooms, and an old gallery-result.txt must stay unchanged during review. These are example files, not assignment files.
teaching.try_change: Replace mode=$1 with mode=save, then Run. The example now writes only gallery-result.txt and prints Gallery saved. Restore mode=$1 to return to read-only review.
